chronology: Separate follow-up after first selector hosted result, before observing this adversarial construction. Original admission prereg immutable.
question: Can a prospective sample-window shingle detector distinguish complete-file structural affinity from adversarial files that preserve identical sampled windows but diverge everywhere else?
construction: Six 72KiB regular files per tree. Both trees share identical three 4KiB probe windows in every file. Family A consists of near-identical sources with one tiny change outside samples; family B substitutes independent high-entropy bytes outside the sampled windows, preserving all sampled bytes. Same modes/mtime/names/count/sizes. No corpus labels supplied to selector.
prediction: Both yield identical positive screen observations despite different unsampled relations, demonstrating sampling alone cannot prove total stored-byte benefit; source-exact full BDC and authentic r24 comparisons price consequences without weakening the original selector.
falsification: Differences in sampled observations, different exact input tree shapes or invalid canonical r24 byte reconstruction invalidate the comparison; canonical size may still win either way, and full-materialized result must control decision.
scope: research-only information-bound falsifier of detector sufficiency. No change to existing selector constants, no new codec/reader grammar, no product credit.
alternative_explanation: Common sampled windows might remain enough to compress even fully independent unsampled regions, in which case classification indistinguishability remains established but adverse size effect is not.
controls: same logical file sizes and POSIX metadata
full canonical r24 archive and Reader verification
complete BDC sibling length with unchanged source
observed BDC code exact Git SHA
